statement: In trapezoid $ABCD$, sides $\overline{AB}$ and $\overline{CD}$ are parallel, and the diagonals $\overline{AC}$ and $\overline{BD}$ meet at $P$. Triangle $BPC$ has area $12$ and triangle $CPD$ has area $4$. What is the area of the trapezoid?

choices.misconception: I correctly found that triangle $APD$ also has area $12$, then added $12 + 12 + 4$ and forgot triangle $APB$ entirely.
I saw that $AP : PC = 3 : 1$ and scaled the area of triangle $CPD$ by $3$ to get $12$ for triangle $APB$, but similar triangles scale area by the square of the ratio.
I found triangle $APB$ has area $36$ but added only $36 + 12 + 4$, leaving out triangle $APD$.
I knew area scales by $9$ but multiplied the area of triangle $BPC$ instead of the similar triangle $CPD$, getting $108$ for triangle $APB$.

hints: Triangles $ABD$ and $ABC$ share the base $\overline{AB}$ and the same height.
Equal-height triangles give $[APD] = [BPC]$. Triangles $BPC$ and $CPD$ share a height from $C$, so their areas give the ratio $BP : PD$.
$BP : PD = 12 : 4 = 3 : 1$, so triangles $APB$ and $CPD$ are similar with ratio $3$ and $[APB] = 9 \cdot 4 = 36$. Add all four pieces.

solutions.reliable: Triangles $ABD$ and $ABC$ have the same base and height, so they have equal area; removing the shared triangle $APB$ gives $[APD] = [BPC] = 12$. Triangles $BPC$ and $DPC$ share the vertex $C$ and bases on line $BD$, so $BP : PD = 12 : 4 = 3 : 1$. Because $AB \parallel CD$, triangle $APB$ is similar to triangle $CPD$ with ratio $BP : PD = 3$, so $[APB] = 9 \cdot 4 = 36$. The trapezoid has area $36 + 12 + 12 + 4 = 64$. Transferable idea: the diagonals of a trapezoid cut it into two similar triangles and two equal side triangles.
solutions.elegant: For the four triangles around $P$, $[APB] \cdot [CPD] = [BPC] \cdot [DPA]$, since both products equal $\tfrac14 \, AP \cdot PC \cdot BP \cdot PD \cdot \sin^2 \angle APB$. So $[APB] = 12 \cdot 12 / 4 = 36$, and the total is $(\sqrt{36} + \sqrt{4})^2 = 64$.

author: Devansh Sanghavi
